verses.text: When Solomon finished praying, fire came down from heaven and burned up the burnt offering and the sacrifices. The glory of the LORD filled the temple.
The priests could not go into the LORD's temple, because the glory of the LORD filled it.

All the people of Israel watched the fire come down and saw the LORD's glory over the temple. They bowed down with their faces to the stone floor. They worshipped and thanked the LORD, singing, "He is good; his faithful love lasts forever!"
Then the king and all the people offered sacrifices before the LORD.
King Solomon sacrificed twenty-two thousand cattle and one hundred and twenty thousand sheep. So the king and all the people dedicated God's temple.

The priests stood in their places. The Levites stood with the LORD's musical instruments that King David had made for praising the LORD, when David gave thanks through their service, singing, "His faithful love lasts forever." Facing the Levites, the priests blew trumpets, and all Israel stood.

Solomon made holy the middle part of the courtyard in front of the LORD's temple. There he offered the burnt offerings and the fat of the peace offerings, because the bronze altar he had made was too small to hold all the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and fat.
At that time Solomon and all Israel with him celebrated the festival for seven days. It was a very large crowd, people from Lebo Hamath in the north all the way to the Brook of Egypt in the south.
On the eighth day they held a special meeting. They had celebrated the dedication of the altar for seven days and the festival for seven days.

On the twenty-third day of the seventh month, Solomon sent the people home. They were joyful and glad in their hearts for all the good things the LORD had done for David, for Solomon, and for his people Israel.
So Solomon finished the LORD's temple and the royal palace. He succeeded in doing everything he had planned for the LORD's temple and for his own palace.
Then the LORD appeared to Solomon at night and said to him, "I have heard your prayer, and I have chosen this place for myself as a temple for sacrifices.
When I shut the sky so there is no rain, or command locusts to eat up the land, or send disease among my people,
if my people, who are called by my name, will humble themselves, pray, seek me, and turn from their wicked ways, then I will hear from heaven. I will forgive their sin and heal their land.
Now my eyes will be open and my ears will listen to the prayers made in this place.
I have chosen this temple and made it holy, so that my name will be there forever. My eyes and my heart will always be there.
As for you, if you follow me as your father David did, and do everything I command, and obey my laws and rules,
then I will make your royal throne secure, as I promised your father David when I said, 'You will always have a descendant to rule over Israel.'
But if you turn away and abandon the laws and commands I have given you, and go and serve and worship other gods,
then I will pull Israel up by the roots from my land that I gave them. I will reject this temple I have made holy for my name. I will make it a joke and an insult among all the nations.
This temple is so impressive now, but everyone who passes by will be shocked and ask, 'Why has the LORD done this to this land and to this temple?'

People will answer, 'Because they abandoned the LORD, the God of their ancestors, who brought them out of Egypt. They chose other gods, worshipping and serving them. That is why he has brought all this disaster on them.'"
